hacker_news.title: Our organizations are being DDoSed from the inside
hacker_news.author: mavelikara
hacker_news.summary: Agents let us generate changes faster than we can understand, review, and decide. How do companies keep the ability to steer?

linked_context.page_title: Our organizations are being DDoSed from the inside
linked_context.page_description: Agents let us generate changes faster than we can understand, review, and decide. How do companies keep the ability to steer?
linked_context.page_excerpt:
I’ve written before that you can outsource work, but not your understanding.

As a CEO, I’m finding that harder to live up to. It feels like our organizations are being DDoSed from the inside. Nobody is trying to overwhelm the company. Everyone is doing something they think is useful. But all of that work draws on the same limited capacity to understand, review, and decide. We can generate changes much faster than we can give them that attention.

I’m trying to keep product and marketing aligned while what we’re building changes daily. By the time I understand something well enough to contribute, the work might have already changed. Teams and agents are moving faster than any of us can follow.

Hi HN, I’m Chris, a solo dev in Sydney.

Spacecamps gives caravan parks and campgrounds their own online booking page, an interactive site map and guest messaging. Parks pay a flat monthly fee (A$59 for up to 100 sites, A$129 for up to 250). There are no commissions or setup fees.

I built it because booking a park spot in Australia can be quite painful. Many parks still want you to ring for availability, and the booking platforms that exist are clunky and outdated. It’s especially bad when you need somewhere for tonight and you’re standing by the road with one bar of reception. I wanted guests to be able to see what’s free and book in a minute, and I wanted parks to keep the money instead of losing a cut on every booking.

It’s built with React Router in framework mode. I spent a lot of time keeping the guest booking portal light, with minimal JavaScript and a small payload, so it loads fast on a weak mobile connection. That’s the exact situation it was built for.

I’d really appreciate feedback, from park operators or from anyone who’s tried to book a campsite on short notice.

hacker_news.title: TimeScore Weighted Scoring Algorithm
hacker_news.author: mckoss
hacker_news.summary: Counting likes ranks what was popular, not what’s popular now. TimeScore lets every like fade with a half-life, and stores each item’s score as one number that never needs updating as time passes. With a live demo, the code, and the patent.
comment_highlights: I've placed my patented social scoring algorithm in the public domain. This site describes how it works (and is much easier to understand than the patent). Code snippets included.

linked_context.page_title: TimeScore: Ranking What's Popular Now | mckoss.com
linked_context.page_description: Counting likes ranks what was popular, not what’s popular now. TimeScore lets every like fade with a half-life, and stores each item’s score as one number that never needs updating as time passes. With a live demo, the code, and the patent.
linked_context.page_excerpt:
Every site that shows a list of “popular” things (stories, links, posts, products, tags) has to decide what popular means. The simplest answer is to count: the item with the most likes, up-votes, clicks or shares is on top.

But counts only grow. An item that collected a thousand likes last month stays ahead of one that fifty people liked in the last hour, and a list ranked by counts fills up with yesterday’s news. What readers usually want is what’s popular now .

TimeScore fixes this by letting every like fade with age. A like is worth one point when it happens, half a point one half-life later, a quarter after two half-lives, and so on. An item’s score is the sum of its faded likes, so the top of the list is whatever has been getting attention lately. And each item’s score is kept as a single number that never has to be updated as time passes.
